# {{cookiecutter.project_name}}

A unified work dashboard for Claude Code: {{cookiecutter.primary_tracker_name}} and GitHub
stay the source of truth for tracked work, and this repo holds everything they don't
(personal tasks, meeting notes, a progress log) plus the index that ties it all
together.

**Do not edit this file** — see `CLAUDE.md` for why (it documents the system, so it
stays generic).

## Files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Operational rules Claude Code follows automatically in this repo |
| `DASHBOARD.md` | Live index of tracked initiatives, key repos, and upcoming deadlines |
| `TASKS.md` | Personal/admin tasks that exist nowhere else, by priority (P1/P2/P3) |
| `PROGRESS.md` | Dated, one-line log of completed work |
| `notes/` | One Markdown file per meeting/event, named `YYYY-MM-DD-title.md` |
| `.claude/settings.json` | Permission allowlist for the MCP tools this workflow relies on |

## Getting started

1. Fill in `DASHBOARD.md` with your actual tracked initiatives and key repos.
2. Point `CLAUDE.md`'s tracker link and key-repo names at your real values (these were
   templated in from cookiecutter — search for anything still generic and update it).
3. Connect your tracker's MCP server. This template ships `.claude/settings.json` with
   only the GitHub MCP tool names allowed, since those apply regardless of which
   tracker you use — it doesn't assume or hardcode Confluence, Jira, Linear, or
   anything else. Getting your own tracker wired up is two separate steps:
   - **Register the server itself with Claude Code.** This template doesn't do this
     for you — follow your tracker's own MCP server setup instructions (a global
     `claude mcp add` entry, or an `.mcp.json` in this repo if you want it scoped
     to this project). Common ones include Atlassian (Confluence/Jira), Linear, and
     Notion, but any MCP server for your actual tracker works.
   - **Allow its tools once it's connected.** Add its tool names (they look like
     `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, e.g. `mcp__atlassian-agent__confluence_get_page`) to
     the `allow` list in `.claude/settings.json`.
   Which server you pick is entirely up to you and your tracker — CLAUDE.md's
   `{{cookiecutter.primary_tracker_name}}` references are generic on purpose, so no
   source is assumed.
4. Ask Claude Code "what should I work on next?" any time — it follows the protocol in
   `CLAUDE.md` to check your tracker and GitHub live, not just this repo's cached index.

## Keeping up with template updates

This project was generated with [cruft](https://cruft.github.io/cruft/). To pull in
improvements made to the upstream template later:

```bash
cruft check    # see if you're behind
cruft update   # pull in the diff
```

`.cruft.json` (created at generation time) tracks which template commit you're on.

## Linting

Markdown is linted with [markdownlint-cli2](https://github.com/DavidAnson/markdownlint-cli2)
(see `.markdownlint.yaml`), run in CI on every push/PR via
`.github/workflows/lint.yml`, and locally via
[pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com) (see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`):

```bash
pre-commit install   # one-time, runs the same checks before each commit
```
